question: Does the conclusion of a three-term argument have to follow from its two premises, and if not, what would a world look like where it fails?
finding: Of the 256 possible syllogistic forms, exhaustive model checking finds 15 valid on the modern reading and 24 once every term is assumed to have at least one member.
limit: Validity is not truth: the tool checks whether the conclusion follows from the premises, not whether the premises are right or the words mean the same thing each time.
